title: The House That Waited
content:
It was already late when Clara's car broke down on a narrow road surrounded by a dark forest.

She had been driving home after visiting her grandmother, but the engine suddenly stopped.

She looked around nervously.

There were no other cars, and her phone battery was too low to call anyone.

In the distance, Clara noticed an old house.

She wasn't sure if it was safe enough to enter, but the night was becoming too cold to stay outside.

Slowly, she walked toward the house and knocked on the large wooden door.

Nobody answered.

Clara waited for a few seconds before she finally decided to go in.

The door opened with a loud sound.

Inside, the house was extremely dark.

Clara turned on her phone's flashlight, but the light wasn't bright enough to illuminate the entire hallway.

— Hello? — she called out quietly.

Her voice came back as an echo.

She began to look for a light switch.

While she was searching, she suddenly came across an old photograph on the wall.

The picture showed a family standing in front of the same house.

Clara looked closer.

One of the people in the photograph looked exactly like her.

She quickly backed away.

— That can't be possible — she whispered.

Suddenly, a loud noise came from upstairs.

Clara wanted to run away, but curiosity was too strong.

She slowly went up the stairs.

Each step was incredibly loud.

At the end of the hallway, she found a small room.

The door was slightly open.

She tried to look inside, but the room was too dark to see anything clearly.

Then she heard someone whisper:

— Clara... you finally came back.

She immediately turned around, but nobody was there.

Her heart was beating too fast, and she wasn't calm enough to think clearly.

She ran downstairs and tried to get out, but the front door wouldn't open.

She pulled the handle again and again, but it was too heavy to move.

Then all the lights suddenly went out.

Clara screamed.

From somewhere behind her, she heard slow footsteps.

She tried to calm down, but she was too terrified to move.

The footsteps came closer.

Then, a hand suddenly touched her shoulder.

Clara turned around slowly.

It was an old woman.

The woman smiled strangely.

— You shouldn't have come in — she said quietly.

Clara looked toward the photograph again.

The family was still there.

But now, there was one more person standing in the picture.

Clara.

And behind her, the old woman was smiling.

The house had been waiting patiently.

And now, Clara was finally close enough to become part of it.
